lesson.title: PINNs for 1D Linear Convection Equation
lesson.goal: train a PINN on the convection equation

steps.title: Import libraries and define PINN
steps.instructions: Define the PINN neural network architecture in pinn_convection.py using linear layers and Tanh activations.

explanations.topic: Setting random seeds for consistent weight initialization and optimization

hints: Start by importing torch, torch.nn, numpy, and matplotlib.pyplot.
Fix the random seeds with torch.manual_seed(42) and np.random.seed(42).
Use nn.ModuleList() inside PINN.__init__ to stack Linear and Tanh layers, ending with a Linear output layer.
common_mistakes: Putting a Tanh activation after the final output Linear layer, which restricts output values to (-1, 1).
Using a plain Python list instead of nn.ModuleList(), which prevents PyTorch from tracking layer parameters.

steps.title: Implement the physics loss function
steps.instructions: Implement pde_residual in pinn_convection.py using torch.autograd.grad to calculate du_dt and du_dx.

explanations.topic: Enabling requires_grad on x_pde and t_pde to compute PDE derivatives
Using grad_outputs and create_graph=True in torch.autograd.grad
Computing and squaring the PDE residual du/dt + c * du/dx

hints: Call requires_grad_(True) on both x_pde and t_pde before passing them to the model.
Concatenate x_pde and t_pde along dim=1 to pass (x, t) pairs into the model.
Use torch.autograd.grad(u, t_pde, grad_outputs=torch.ones_like(u), create_graph=True)[0] for each partial derivative.
common_mistakes: Forgetting requires_grad_(True) on x_pde and t_pde, causing autograd.grad to raise a RuntimeError.
Omitting create_graph=True, which prevents backpropagation through the PDE residual loss during training.
Forgetting [0] after torch.autograd.grad(), which returns a tuple instead of a tensor.

steps.title: Write the PINN training loop
steps.instructions: Implement sample_points in pinn_convection.py to sample random domain points with autograd gradient tracking.

explanations.topic: Evaluating the model at t=0 with torch.zeros_like(x_ic) for initial condition loss
Combining IC and PDE losses and computing parameter gradients with total_loss.backward()

hints: Clear gradients at the start of every epoch using optimizer.zero_grad().
Pass torch.cat((x_ic, torch.zeros_like(x_ic)), dim=1) to evaluate u at t=0.
Sample x_pde and t_pde uniformly over their min/max bounds using torch.rand(num_pde_points, 1).
common_mistakes: Forgetting optimizer.zero_grad(), causing gradients to accumulate across epochs.
Misaligning tensor shapes between x_ic and torch.zeros_like(x_ic) when calling torch.cat.

steps.title: Configure domain and run training
steps.instructions: Run pinn_convection.py with beta=1.0 in the terminal to train the PINN model.

targets.caption: Train the PINN on the convection equation

explanations.topic: Sampling initial condition points and 10,000 PDE collocation points across the domain
First-order Adam optimizer vs quasi-second-order L-BFGS in PINNs

hints: Reshape torch.linspace(x_min, x_max, num_ic_points) with .view(-1, 1) so it is a column tensor.
Compute the analytical solution at t=1.0 using np.exp(-10 * (x - c * 1.0)**2) to verify the PINN curve.
common_mistakes: Passing a 1D tensor instead of shape (N, 1) for x_ic, which breaks torch.cat along dim=1.
Forgetting to switch the model to model.eval() and torch.no_grad() when evaluating predictions for plotting.

steps.title: Test negative convection speed
steps.instructions: Run pinn_convection.py with --beta -1.0 in the terminal to evaluate training with negative convection velocity.

targets.caption: Train PINN with negative convection speed

explanations.topic: Checking whether PINNs are sensitive to wave propagation direction unlike numerical upwinding

hints: Update the convection speed variable from c = 1.0 to c = -1.0.
Make sure the analytical solution formula also uses the variable c rather than a hardcoded +1.0.
common_mistakes: Changing c to -1.0 for training while leaving the analytical comparison hardcoded to c = 1.0.

steps.title: Train on sharper Gaussian IC
steps.instructions: Run pinn_convection.py with --beta 2.0 to test model training under higher convection speeds.

targets.caption: Train PINN with higher convection speed

explanations.topic: How PINNs capture sharp Gaussian pulses without fine-grid discretization errors

hints: Set hidden_dim = 30 and restore c = 1.0 with domain bounds -1.0 to 2.0.
Use beta = 500 in both u_ic and the analytical solution formula.
common_mistakes: Updating the IC to exp(-500*x^2) while leaving the analytical comparison curve at -10.

steps.title: Compare with non-dimensionalized PINN
steps.instructions: Run a full training run of pinn_convection.py for 4000 epochs to verify convergence.

explanations.topic: Defining characteristic scales L_c, T_c, and U_c to normalize variables
Comparing dimensional and non-dimensionalized PINN predictions at t=1.0

hints: Set L_c = 1.0 / np.sqrt(beta) and T_c = L_c / c so the non-dimensional wave speed becomes 1.0.
Divide the dimensional x and t bounds by L_c and T_c respectively.
Use u_ic_nd = torch.exp(-x_ic_nd**2) since beta is absorbed into L_c.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to rescale the non-dimensional evaluation coordinates (x / L_c, t / T_c) when comparing against the dimensional analytical solution at t=1.0.
Keeping beta in u_ic_nd = torch.exp(-x_ic_nd**2) after already scaling x by 1/sqrt(beta).
